registration: Run the same solver once on 4 design clips then one same-subject validation and one repeated subject-disjoint test clip, with frozen weights, geometry, split and anchor identification. Historical subject 11 was previously measured in v160. No new test-selected settings or clips.
source_support: Use frozen CMU 120->50Hz per-foot low (<3.5cm above the human clip floor) and quiet (<0.2 m/s) optical marker criterion. Infer lock by >=4 contiguous frames; never present as measured GRF. For each lock, use the median uncorrected XY of the same lowest median capsule endpoint. No ball target or guessed strike time/pruning.
representation: Retain full marker-derived pelvis orientation and time; optimize root xyz and all 29 joint angles together for every frame on the original G1. Four sequential sparse QPs with all original sole capsule endpoint clearances, per-edge original joint limit, measured human 18 direction terms, temporal derivative preservation, and root and pose priors. No scalar per-frame height shifting.
physics_selection: First train clip with continuous fast outgoing optical ball marker (clip 10_02). Run original and newly optimized once each in same 14s PAiD and default real moving ball/goal configuration. Hit and instep not required or inferred from source. Initial source first frame and complete-clip then last-frame hold identical treatment.
acceptance: Primary: fewer >=1 cm penetration frames and reduced maximum penetration, lower median of per-clip p95 anchored material speed; no increased support >20mm hover count; mean anatomical direction error <=3 degrees and mean direction-rate cosine nondegradation <=0.05. Report support hover, ankle and material speeds, all 18 direction errors, original q/v bounds, acceleration and individual clips including all failures. Independent held-out subject not a project-first discovery.
scope: Low/quiet support and capsule contacts are geometric proxies. Dynamic forces, true contact phase, professional player quality, physical realizability, and learned coordination remain unverified. Constant foot anchors may suppress genuine toe/heel roll and cannot replace force plates.
